react_result.final_narrative_text: A multi-paradigm metabolomics enrichment analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites reveals a dominant disruption of amino-acid one-carbon metabolism, anchored on the KEGG pathway 'Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism' (KEGG:hsa00260). This pathway achieved the top rank in three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁹), mummichog m/z-direct activity (p = 5.88 × 10⁻⁴, 14 of 14 compounds overlapped), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 2.12 × 10⁻⁸). Seven driver metabolites are directly embedded in this pathway roster: glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), O-phospho-L-serine (KEGG:C01005), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), guanidinoacetic acid (KEGG:C00581), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00021), and L-cystathionine (KEGG:C02291). The convergent signal across ORA (hypergeometric over-representation), empirical-compound network activity (m/z matching), and pathway-set enrichment (PSEA) confirms this as a robust, method-independent finding. A secondary hit — Methionine and cysteine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00480) — appears in both mummichog and MetaboAnalystR, consistent with the known metabolic branch point between the serine/glycine axis and the methionine cycle (shared intermediates: SAH, L-cysteine, L-cystathionine). Niacinamide (KEGG:C00153), while not a direct member of hsa00260, participates in the NAD⁺ salvage axis and surfaced in the Vitamin B3 mummichog module, suggesting a co-occurring NAD⁺-depletion stress in the treatment condition.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms identified amino acid metabolism as the dominant affected sector. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) was the top KEGG hit in the RaMP ORA with FDR 1.27×10⁻¹⁹ and 8 metabolite hits, and rank 2 in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA with p=2.12×10⁻⁸. The Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis returned Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism as its top pathway. Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders (WP:WP4292) ranked 11 in RaMP ORA (FDR 5.67×10⁻¹³) and appeared in the Mummichog result as Methionine and cysteine metabolism. The broad parent pathway Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (REACT:R-HSA-71291) was the top hit in the Reactome namespace with FDR 1.37×10⁻²² and 11 metabolite hits. Glycine occupies a central position in this metabolite set, appearing in both the glycine-serine-threonine axis and the methionine-cysteine-sulfur axis via intermediates cystathionine and S-adenosylhomocysteine.
